A.explanation: PQ is from the centre of a compression at P to the centre of the next rarefaction at Q, which is only half a wavelength.

B.explanation: PS is from a compression centre at P to a rarefaction centre at S, which is one and a half wavelengths, not one.

C.explanation: QR is from a rarefaction centre at Q to the next compression centre at R, which is only half a wavelength.

D.explanation: QS is from the centre of one rarefaction at Q to the centre of the next rarefaction at S, which is one full wavelength.

hints: Look at where the dots are crowded together and where they are spread out to locate the centres of compression and rarefaction marked by P, Q, R and S.
Recall that wavelength $\lambda$ for a longitudinal wave is the distance between two successive points oscillating in phase, such as compression to compression or rarefaction to rarefaction.
Check which pair in the options joins two Q-type sparse regions or two P-type dense regions separated by one full repeat of the pattern.
walkthrough: Identify the pattern in the dot diagram: dense dots are compressions and sparse dots are rarefactions of the longitudinal sound wave.
Locate the markers: P and R are at the centres of successive compressions, while Q and S are at the centres of successive rarefactions.
State the rule: wavelength $\lambda$ is the distance between two successive identical points in phase, so compression to next compression or rarefaction to next rarefaction.
Compare the options: PQ and QR each join a compression to a rarefaction, so each is $\lambda / 2$.
Note that QS joins the rarefaction at Q to the very next rarefaction at S, which is one complete repeat of the wave. This is option D.
